html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation

  • What the context window is and why long chats degrade
  • The difference between length limits and usage limits
  • When to restart, summarize or persist
  • How memory, chat search and Projects carry context, and how to control them

2The Context Window

Running case

Cedarbrook's Marathon Chat

  • A planner works on the holiday-season plan in one chat for three days
  • Early decisions get forgotten, the answers repeat themselves, and finally Claude warns that the message will exceed the length limit

The context window is everything Claude can consider in one chat: your messages, its replies, uploaded files, tool results and instructions. It is finite.

  • Length limit = how long a single conversation can get. The newest models on paid plans support very large windows (up to about 1 million tokens; others 500K or 200K) [Verify live]; part of the window is reserved for the reply.
  • Usage limit = how much you can use Claude over time (a five-hour session limit and weekly limits on paid plans). The two are different: a short chat can hit a usage limit, and a long chat can hit a length limit.
  • Automatic context management (with code execution on): when a chat nears the limit, Claude summarizes earlier messages so the chat can continue; your full history stays available. Longer chats still use more of your usage limit.
  • What fills the window: long chats, large attachments, many tool results, and every connector's tool definitions.
  • Symptoms of a crowded context: forgotten early instructions, contradictions, repetition, slower and weaker answers, the error "Your message will exceed the length limit for this chat".
Exam tip

A long chat that has drifted is fixed by managing the context (restart with a summary), not by repeating the same request or hoping for a bigger window.

3Restart, Summarize or Persist

Choice Use when How
Restart (new chat) The topic changes; the chat is very long, drifted or built on a wrong assumption; you hit a length limit Open a new chat; paste only what is needed
Summarize You want to keep decisions but shed the bulk Ask Claude: "Summarize decisions, open questions and key facts so I can continue in a new chat"; check the summary, then paste it into the new chat
Persist You will need the same facts repeatedly Put them in a Project (instructions and knowledge), memory, an artifact or a saved document; do not rely on one long thread
  • A handoff summary should list decisions made, constraints, definitions, open items and the next step. Review it: summaries can drop numbers and commitments.
  • Persist the stable, summarize the changing. Brand voice and policy go in a Project; the state of today's task goes in a short summary.
  • Starting fresh also cuts usage: a shorter chat costs less per message.
  • Editing an earlier message creates a separate branch, so you can try another direction without losing the first.

4Memory and Chat Search

Feature What it does Controls
Memory Claude stores useful facts as individual topics (role, projects, preferences, ongoing work) and uses them in later chats On by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; pause (stop using and creating), reset (delete all, cannot be undone), edit or delete topics in Settings, or ask Claude to forget something
Chat search (paid plans) Finds relevant past chats when you ask "What did we decide about X?" Turn off "Search and reference chats" in Settings
Project memory Each Project has its own memory, separate from other Projects "Use account memory" off on the Project page fully separates it; deleted with the Project
Memory off for one chat Start a chat without memory Turn off Memory in the "+" menu before the first message; it cannot be changed afterward; the chat stays in history
Incognito chat A temporary chat: not saved to history, not used for memory, not used for model training Ghost icon; outside Projects only; kept for 30 days by default for safety even though hidden; cannot be reopened after closing

  • What memory keeps: your role and projects, working preferences, people and places in your work, technical preferences.
  • Sensitive topics (for example health, politics, religion) are off by default in memory. You can opt in; turning it off later removes saved sensitive items.
  • Never saved, even on request: government ID numbers, criminal history, financial account numbers, immigration status.
  • Deleting a conversation does not delete the memories made from it. Delete the memory topic itself.
  • Memory carries over; do not rely on it for facts you must always have. For must-have rules, put them in Project instructions (Module 11).
  • On Team and Enterprise, owners control whether memory is available but cannot read individual users' memories; turning memory off for the organization deletes everyone's memory.
  • Import and export of memory from other assistants is possible but experimental; memory focuses on work-related topics.
  • In Projects, large knowledge uses RAG: Claude retrieves only the relevant parts, so a Project can hold up to about 10 times more than fits in context (paid plans).
Exam tip

"Persist" answers use Projects, memory or saved documents; "restart" answers apply when a thread has drifted or grown huge; "summarize" is the bridge between them. Incognito is for privacy from your own history, not for exemption from company policy.

Exam tip

A new chat is not a failure: restart with a short summary when a thread has drifted, and keep stable facts in a Project.

5Exam Q&A

S1A planner's three-day chat now forgets early decisions and repeats itself. What is the best action?

  • ADelete the account and create a fresh one so that the memory starts again from nothing at all
  • BTurn off memory
  • CKeep adding messages
  • DAsk Claude for a summary of decisions and open items, check it, and continue in a new chat
Show the answer

Answer: D. Summarizing and restarting sheds the clutter while keeping the decisions.

S2A team repeats the same 20-page brand guide in every chat. What is the best way to persist it?

  • AAsk Claude to recall it from the last chat
  • BPrint it
  • CAdd it to a Project's knowledge and instructions
  • DPaste it again each time
Show the answer

Answer: C. Stable reference material that is needed repeatedly belongs in a Project's knowledge, not in a long chat that will be lost.

S3What is the difference between a length limit and a usage limit?

  • AA length limit applies to the whole company at once, while a usage limit applies only to single files
  • BThey are the same
  • CA length limit applies to one conversation's context; a usage limit applies to your use over time
  • DA usage limit applies only to files
Show the answer

Answer: C. Length is per conversation; usage is over time (five-hour and weekly limits on paid plans).

S4An employee wants a one-off chat that is not saved to history or memory and not used for training. Which feature fits?

  • AA new Project
  • BAn incognito chat (outside a Project)
  • CChat search through your older conversations
  • DPause memory in Settings
Show the answer

Answer: B. Incognito chats are temporary, not saved to history or memory, and not used for training.

S5A user deletes a conversation that contained a personal detail Claude had saved as memory. What is true?

  • AThe memory is moved to a Project automatically once the conversation is deleted
  • BThe memory is shared with the team
  • CThe memory topic can remain and should be deleted from the memory settings
  • DThe memory is deleted automatically together with the conversation that it came from
Show the answer

Answer: C. Deleting a chat does not delete the memories generated from it.

S6Which TWO belong in "persist" rather than in a chat? Select TWO.

  • AThe brand voice guide used weekly
  • BA one-time question about lunch
  • CThe standard return-policy wording that agents use daily
  • DA draft that you will discard
  • EToday's rough brainstorm that will not be reused
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Reused reference material goes into a Project or saved document.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Context window Everything Claude considers in a chat; finite
Length vs usage Length = one conversation; usage = over time (five-hour and weekly)
Auto management Older messages summarized near the limit; more usage
Restart Topic change, drift, wrong assumption, very long chat
Summarize Decisions, constraints, open items, next step; check it
Persist Projects, memory, artifacts, saved documents
Memory On by default (individual plans); pause, reset, edit, per-chat off
Project memory Separate per Project
Incognito Not saved, no memory, no training; outside Projects; kept 30 days
Sensitive topics Off by default; some items never saved
